payload.text: The thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery originated at the Brennecke Institute. Its dopant reduces electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Cycling must be suspended below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
